pages.title: Sans-IO Decision Core
pages.purpose: The celld-logic sans-IO decision core: the on_event/Event/Effect contract, State ownership, the subsystem map (gates, routing, restore, pressure, wake, drain, isolate, log tiers, cache), and how determinism is used for validation
instructions: Map each logic submodule to the decision it owns and the adapter that executes it.
State uncertainty about where simulation/TLA+ harnesses live; they are not in this snapshot.

pages.title: Node Runtime and Actor Loop
pages.purpose: Node process: startup and listener binding, the serial Actor event loop and effect adapters, the asyncrt execution facade, machine/host-services sampling, strict env parsing, and the clippy enforcement boundary
instructions: Cover why monotonic lease ticks survive hung storage operations.
Explain the boundary lints and the facade rather than listing every forbidden path.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: System map: what celld is, the three-crate ownership split (pure decision core, effect-executor host, replication library), and the end-to-end request and write data flows
instructions: Describe ownership boundaries, not file inventories.
Trace one cold request and one durable write end to end across the crates.

pages.title: Cells, Ownership, and Fencing
pages.purpose: Cell lifecycle and ownership: resident/active/idle/hibernated/inactive states, bucket ownership records and conditional claims, fencing epochs, activation/takeover/release paths, routing retry semantics, hibernated WebSockets, alarms and cron-driven wakes
instructions: Cover alarm wake (crates/celld/wake.rs, crates/logic/wake.rs) and cron cells here.
Ground epoch/fencing claims in the record formats and logic code, not only in docs prose.

pages.title: Cloudflare Compatibility Surface
pages.purpose: Cloudflare Workers/Durable Objects compatibility: the conformance contract, supported services and bindings (DO, KV, D1, Queues, Workflows, R2, assets, cron, service bindings), reserved __-prefixed class cells, known gaps, and the examples/ corpus
instructions: Map each supported service to the reserved-cell implementation in logic/celld.
Use docs/cloudflare-compat.md status tables as the compatibility contract.

pages.title: Durability and the RPO=0 Protocol
pages.purpose: Durability and fencing protocol: the output gate rule, RPO=0 acknowledgement with ownership re-check, bucket vs fleet (node-log ensemble) proofs, takeover recovery gate, full-prefix restore, self-fencing and exit behavior
instructions: Do not invent latency or consistency guarantees beyond cited measurements.
Separate what the code enforces from what docs/guarantees.md asserts.

pages.title: Listeners and Peer Networking
pages.purpose: Listener surface and peer networking: public Worker listener routes, internal listener routes (/state, /reload, /shutdown, peer routes), the pooled peer tunnel carrying plain HTTP, fleet HMAC signing/replay protection, protocol versioning, and WebSocket accept/proxy/outbound paths
instructions: Cover both directions: inbound proxying and outbound client sockets.
State clearly that peer traffic is unencrypted HTTP on a trusted network; the code does not terminate TLS.

pages.title: SQLite State and LTX Replication
pages.purpose: SQLite state and LTX replication: per-cell databases behind the DO storage API, WAL capture as LTX segments, the ltx crate architecture (db/replica/compactor/bundles), L0/L1/L9 compaction and snapshots, epoch-prefixed bucket layout, restore chain reading
instructions: Cover the ltx crate as a library with its own restore/compaction APIs.
Use crates/ltx/reference/ltx-format.md for format claims.

pages.title: Workers and V8 Runtime
pages.purpose: The Workers execution engine: rusty_v8 embedding in js.rs, the JS bootstrap/harness and Web/node API surface, isolate pool scheduling and heap limits, DO storage/WebSocket/crypto bindings, WebAssembly modules, and deployment generations (build/adopt/drain)
instructions: Distinguish Worker-scope versus cell-scope execution surfaces.
List js/ built-in modules as evidence of the web-compat surface, not file by file.

pages.title: Build and Release Pipeline
pages.purpose: Building and releasing: workspace layout and profile strategy (release/lab/dev crypto overrides), the lint gates that encode architecture boundaries, Dockerfile multi-stage build and test stage, and the two-phase GitHub Actions release with attestations
instructions: Do not assume CI behavior beyond what release.yml shows.
Explain what each release profile trades and which artifact is shipped.

pages.title: Deploy and Local Development
pages.purpose: Deploying and developing applications: how celld deploy builds a Wrangler project with esbuild and publishes manifest/pointer objects to the bucket, the protocol.rs bucket contract, in-place generation adoption and /reload, and the celld dev local stack with its SQLite-backed local object store and watcher
instructions: Cover both the deploy pipeline and the local dev loop.
Document the bucket object contract (protocol.rs types and key layout) as the integration seam.

pages.title: Fleet Operations
pages.purpose: Operating a fleet: configuration surface and env-variable contract, object-storage provider dialects and credential rules, startup storage probe, graceful shutdown with drain token and batched handoff, first-readiness gate, memory-pressure shedding and resident caps, version-upgrade constraints, and diagnose
instructions: Cite defaults from code where the docs table and env_vars.rs agree, and note where only docs state them.
Do not invent deployment topology beyond README/Docker examples.

pages.title: Observability and Control Plane
pages.purpose: Observability: node logs and structured events, the wide-event telemetry pipeline with Parquet-to-bucket and hand-written OTLP sinks, sampling and drop-on-saturation behavior, health and /state endpoints, and the celld.dev managed control-plane integration
instructions: Cover the managed control-plane session (control_plane.rs) as an alpha external integration.
Note the off-by-default structural argument for telemetry.

pages.title: Operator CLIs
pages.purpose: Operator command surface: shared fleet flag parsing and the stdout/stderr Output boundary, the signed /runtime operator path in operator_cell.rs, and the cell list, d1, kv, and queue subcommands
instructions: Cover the stdout/stderr data-vs-message separation rule.
Explain why operators go through a node rather than the bucket (fence safety).

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: build and run the node from source, celld dev, deploy, first fleet command, and where to change common things
instructions: Point to the narrowest owning source file for each maintenance task.
Verify every command against README.md, docs/README.md, and crates/celld/main/cli.rs help text; do not invent flags.
